label: Supplier requests (today, real time)
purpose: Today's requests from the GTE booking engine to suppliers, refreshed through the day: volumes, hotels asked and returned, cache use, look-to-book, response times and outcomes. It holds the current day only.
grain: Supplier requests aggregated per hour and 10-minute slot of today (UAE time and CET), supplier connection, client, credential, interface, request type and context, availability type, cache flag, response-time band and outcome.
use_for: supplier traffic today, this hour or right now
today's supplier response times, errors and time-outs by supplier
live monitoring of a supplier connection during the day
not_for: yesterday or any earlier period (Statistics History Supplier)
full-day totals for today before the day is over (the day is still in progress)
requests clients send to GTE (Statistics Real Time Client)

coverage.note: Real time: only the current day (UAE time), loaded with about an hour's delay. On 2026-10-16 at about 17:00 UAE time it held 2026-10-16, hours 00 to 16. Each day replaces the previous one, so there is no history and 'last 12 months' totals are empty by design.

dates.label: Request date (UAE time)
dates.meaning: Day the request was sent to the supplier, in UAE time (UTC+4). The cube's main date; it only ever holds today.

dates.label: Request date (UAE time, copy)
dates.meaning: Same request date as 'Calendario'[Fecha] in a separate table (identical figures); prefer 'Calendario'[Fecha].

dates.label: Request date (CET)
dates.meaning: request_date_cet = the request date in Central European time (2 hours behind UAE in summer, 3 in winter). Use only when CET is asked.

dates.label: Request date (CET, copy)
dates.meaning: Same CET request date as 'Calendar CET'[Date CET] in a separate table; prefer 'Calendar CET'[Date CET].

dates.label: Same date last year (CET)
dates.meaning: Last-year helper: CET request date shifted one year. Never use in questions; the app compares periods itself.

dates.label: Same weekday last year (CET)
dates.meaning: Last-year helper aligned on weekday. Never use in questions.

measures.name: [Requests]
measures.label: Supplier requests
measures.definition: Number of request messages the booking engine sent to suppliers (availability, cancellation policy, booking, etc.).
measures.notes: Main measure. Billions per month; use with 'Tipo Fallos'[Fallo] for errors, time-outs and no results.

measures.name: [Hotels Request]
measures.label: Hotels requested from suppliers
measures.definition: Number of hotels asked for in the supplier requests (one request can ask for many hotels).

measures.name: [AVG Hotels Request]
measures.label: Average hotels per supplier request
measures.definition: [Hotels Request] / [Requests]: hotels asked per supplier request.
terms: average hotels per supplier request today

measures.name: [Hotel Results]
measures.label: Hotels returned by suppliers
measures.definition: Number of hotels the suppliers returned with availability.

measures.name: [AVG Hotel Results]
measures.label: Average hotels returned per supplier request
measures.definition: [Hotel Results] / [Requests]: hotels with availability returned per supplier request.
terms: average hotels returned per supplier request today

measures.name: [% Hotel Results]
measures.label: Supplier hotel result rate
measures.definition: [Hotel Results] / [Hotels Request]: share of the hotels asked that suppliers returned with availability.
measures.notes: Verified ratio of the two counts.

measures.name: [Hotels Cached]
measures.label: Hotels served from cache
measures.definition: Hotels answered from GTE's cache instead of a live supplier call (only where 'Request Cached' = Yes).

measures.name: [% Hotels Cached]
measures.label: Supplier cache hit rate
measures.definition: [Hotels Cached] / [Hotels Request]: share of the hotels asked that were served from cache.
measures.notes: Verified ratio; values around 0.01%, hence 3 decimals.

measures.name: [L2B]
measures.label: Supplier look-to-book
measures.definition: Look-to-book ratio: supplier requests per booking ([Requests] / bookings). Exact inverse of [% L2B].
measures.notes: Not a count despite its integer format: values are about 1 million requests per booking and not whole numbers. The booking count behind it is not exposed. Only valid without request-context / outcome breakdowns (see rules).

measures.name: [% L2B]
measures.label: Supplier booking conversion
measures.definition: Bookings per supplier request (bookings / [Requests]), the inverse of [L2B], as a fraction.
measures.notes: Tiny values (about 0.0001%); prefer [L2B] when presenting look-to-book.

measures.name: [AVG Response Time Sec]
measures.label: Average supplier response time
measures.definition: Average time suppliers took to answer a request, in seconds.
measures.notes: Verified in seconds (requests in the '1 - 2' band average 1.4). The cube's own format shows 0 decimals; about 0.4 s overall.

measures.name: [Max Response Time Sec]
measures.label: Maximum supplier response time
measures.definition: Longest time a supplier took to answer a request, in seconds.
measures.notes: It was 120 s on the day read (slowest time-outs); not comparable with the history cube's 180 s cap.

breakdowns.label: Supplier code
breakdowns.meaning: Supplier connection code: how supplier-side cubes identify a supplier.

breakdowns.label: Supplier connection
breakdowns.meaning: Name of the supplier connection the request was sent to (not the same naming as the Bookings cube).

breakdowns.label: Client
breakdowns.meaning: Client (agency, integrator or B2C site) whose activity triggered the supplier request.

breakdowns.label: Client code
breakdowns.meaning: Client code; the safest key to match clients with other cubes.

breakdowns.label: Client market
breakdowns.meaning: Commercial market of the client.
sample_values: GCC - Except UAE and Local Residence

breakdowns.label: Client category
breakdowns.meaning: Client category.

breakdowns.label: Agency group
breakdowns.meaning: Client's agency (pricing) group.

breakdowns.label: Master agency
breakdowns.meaning: Parent agency of the client.

breakdowns.label: Integrator
breakdowns.meaning: Technology integrator the client connects through.

breakdowns.label: Client country
breakdowns.meaning: Country of the client.

breakdowns.label: Credential
breakdowns.meaning: Login/credential used for the request.

breakdowns.label: Interface
breakdowns.meaning: Client channel that triggered the supplier request: XML (client API, almost all traffic), WEB or CLC.

breakdowns.label: Request type
breakdowns.meaning: Kind of call sent to the supplier. Almost all traffic is Availability.

breakdowns.label: Booking-flow step
breakdowns.meaning: Step of the client's booking flow during which the supplier was called.

breakdowns.label: Integrator context
breakdowns.meaning: What the client integration was doing: full or single availability, valuation, booking, cache robots, downloads. Most traffic is 'Other'.

breakdowns.label: Availability type
breakdowns.meaning: Scope of the availability search: one hotel, several hotels or a whole zone.

breakdowns.label: Outcome
breakdowns.meaning: Result of the supplier request: correct, no results (no availability), supplier error or time-out.

breakdowns.label: Error detail
breakdowns.meaning: Detailed error reason (about 250 texts).

breakdowns.label: Response-time band
breakdowns.meaning: Supplier response time band in seconds ('0 - 1', '1 - 2', ... '> 180', 'Timeout'); sort by its order column.

breakdowns.label: Answered from cache
breakdowns.meaning: Whether the request was answered from GTE's cache.

breakdowns.label: Via rate-optimisation tool
breakdowns.meaning: Yes when the request came through a third-party webservice administrator (rate re-checking tool).

breakdowns.label: Webservice administrator
breakdowns.meaning: Third-party webservice administrator (rate re-checking tool) that made the request; 'Unknown' = none.

breakdowns.label: Hour (UAE time)
breakdowns.meaning: Hour of day of the request, UAE time ('00'-'23').

breakdowns.label: Hour (CET)
breakdowns.meaning: Hour of day of the request, Central European time ('00'-'23').

breakdowns.label: 10-minute slot
breakdowns.meaning: 10-minute slot within the hour ('0 - 9' ... '50 - 59').

named_filters.name: successful supplier requests
named_filters.meaning: Supplier answered correctly (with or without many results).

named_filters.name: supplier no results
named_filters.meaning: Supplier answered but had no availability.

named_filters.name: supplier time-outs
named_filters.meaning: Supplier did not answer in time.

named_filters.name: supplier errors
named_filters.meaning: Supplier returned an error or timed out (excludes 'No results', which is a valid answer).

named_filters.name: supplier booking requests
named_filters.meaning: Booking calls sent to suppliers (calls, not confirmed bookings).

named_filters.name: xml client traffic to suppliers
named_filters.meaning: Supplier requests triggered by clients' XML API.

rules: This is supplier-side traffic (GTE -> suppliers). Requests clients send to GTE are in the client statistics cubes, and searches are in Statistics Zone; never mix them.
Use this cube only for 'today', 'this hour', 'right now' or 'so far today' questions. Any other date has no data here: use Statistics History Supplier (which ends yesterday).

Today's figures are partial (the day is in progress). Never compare them with a full previous day; compare with the same hours of an earlier day from Statistics History Supplier (filter 'Horas'[Hora]) and say so.
Do not put a date filter other than today; a period like 'this month' must come from Statistics History Supplier plus today from this cube, and only additive measures may be combined that way.
The last-year date columns exist but the cube holds no last-year data; never use them.

'Calendario'[Fecha] and 'Horas'[Hora] are UAE time (UTC+4); 'Calendar CET'[Date CET] and 'Horas CET'[Hora] are Central European time (2 hours behind UAE in summer, 3 in winter). Use the UAE pair unless CET is asked, and never mix a UAE date with CET hours.

Suppliers are identified by their connection code 'Suppliers'[Supplier Code] (always with 'Suppliers'[Supplier Code.UniqueName]); 'Suppliers'[Supplier] is the connection's name. The Bookings cube names suppliers differently: joining supplier-side figures to Bookings is by name only and may not match well, so say so whenever you combine them.

Only [Requests], [Hotels Request], [Hotel Results] and [Hotels Cached] add up. Averages, percentages, [L2B], [% L2B] and [Max Response Time Sec] must never be summed or averaged across rows, days or suppliers: query them at the level needed.

[L2B] = [Requests] / bookings (supplier requests per booking) and [% L2B] is its exact inverse. Bookings belong to particular request contexts, so never group or filter L2B by 'Integrator Context', 'Tipo Peticion', 'Context', 'Tipo Fallos', 'Intervalo', 'Request Cached' or 'Availability Type' (it becomes meaningless, e.g. equal to the request count where no booking happened). By date, supplier and client attributes it is fine.

[Requests] counts request messages; [Hotels Request] counts hotels asked (about 5 per request). Neither equals the Statistics Hotel Supplier cube's [Total Hotel Requests] (hotel level, different scope).
Use the cube's measures only; never SUM a column.

review.question: When a question compares today's supplier traffic with an earlier day, should the earlier day be cut to the same hours as today?
review.why: Today is partial (loaded up to about an hour ago); comparing with a full day always shows a false drop.
